title: CobaltBank inference POC — orientation, success metrics & acceptance
body:
Purpose:
This doc captures the orientation plan, measurable success metrics, acceptance criteria, and responsibilities for the CobaltBank inference POC. Goal: validate Redwood’s hosted and dedicated inference options for regulated financial document summarization and customer support triage, and provide a recommended production deployment pattern.

High-level objectives:
- Demonstrate 3 example flows end-to-end: (1) secure doc ingestion + extractive summarization, (2) chat-based triage for support tickets, (3) reranking of candidate responses for compliance review.
- Prove latency and cost envelopes for both Hosted API and Dedicated pools with the customer’s dataset and realistic QPS profiles.
- Validate data residency and audit/logging requirements for CobaltBank (no PII in hosted logs unless encrypted and retained per policy).
- Produce an ops-ready handoff with a concise rollout plan and rollback triggers.

Scope (in-scope):
- Connectors: SFTP drop and S3 ingest of redacted historical customer-support transcripts
- Models: Redwood-verified open model family (quantized variant) + fallback to smaller low-latency model
- Features: streaming responses, token-level cost reporting, per-request redaction hook, and function/tool-calling for structured output
- Observability: per-route latency heatmaps, cost per 1k tokens, and error traces for 95th percentile failures

Out-of-scope:
- Full integration with CobaltBank’s case management UI (only API contract and sample client will be delivered)
- Production capacity reservations beyond a short Dedicated proof window

Success metrics (quantitative):
- Latency: 95th percentile generation latency <= 450ms for support triage median prompt (seq len ~256) on Dedicated during 50 QPS burst window
- Throughput: sustain 70 QPS across the triage route for 30 minutes without >1% request error rate
- Cost: unit inference cost within 30% of the estimate in the commercial proposal for representative workloads
- Accuracy/quality: for summarization, ROUGE-L F1 >= 0.42 on redacted test set (evaluation harness provided); for triage, top-1 intent classification precision >= 0.88 compared to labeled dev set
- Privacy/compliance: no plaintext customer identifiers stored in hosted logs; audit trail shows KMS-wrapped log writes for any persisted artifacts
- Reliability: can failover from primary region to fallback within 90s with <0.5% request loss during a simulated region outage test

Acceptance criteria (must all be satisfied for POC signoff):
1) Functional validation: three demo scenarios run end-to-end with sample customer data and automated test scripts (see linked evaluation artifacts).
2) Non-functional SLOs met: latency, throughput, cost and reliability metrics above validated in dedicated run sessions and synthetic load tests.
3) Security & compliance checklist passed by CobaltBank SecOps (listed checks below) and an agreement on necessary mitigations for anything flagged.
4) Ops handoff: runbook, rollback plan, and contact list delivered; at least one Canary/A/B rollout configured in Redwood Console with automatic fallback policy.
5) Knowledge transfer: 2-hour workshop with CobaltBank eng + 1 hour of runbook walkthrough recorded and stored in S3.

Security & compliance checks (initial):
- Data flow diagram accepted by CobaltBank SecOps (artifact: CONFLUENCE link above)
- KMS integration validated for any persisted artifacts and cache dumps
- No PII in logs unless explicitly authorized and encrypted; dev logs scrubbed by default pipeline
- Attestation for background model weights (list of model sources and checksums provided)

Proposed timeline (3 weeks POC window):
Week 0 (pre-work, 3 business days):
- Kickoff meeting, gather sample datasets, agree on redaction rules (owner: CobaltBank eng lead)
- Provision short-lived Dedicated pool option (if customer opts) and temporary credentials (owner: Redwood infra)

Week 1 (integration & baseline):
- Set up ingest connectors, baseline Hosted API tests, run first eval pass (owner: SE eng)
- Deliver initial latency/cost report on Hosted variant, note hotspots

Week 2 (load tests & tuning):
- Dedicated run (if provisioned): run 50/70 QPS soak tests, measure 95p latency, adjust batching/quantization profile (owner: serving-runtime + SE)
- Run compliance checklist with CobaltBank SecOps

Week 3 (handoff & signoff):
- Final demo with CobaltBank stakeholders, present evaluation results, propose production deployment pattern (hosted vs dedicated vs private)
- Signoff meeting; capture any follow-on engineering work into JIRA backlog

Responsibilities (RACI-lite):
- CobaltBank: provide redacted sample dataset, SecOps reviewer, PO for acceptance decisions
- Redwood SE: integration, eval harness, tuning recommendations, workshop
- Redwood Infra/Platform: provision Dedicated capacity, KMS configuration, networking guidance for Private option
- Customer Success: SLA paperwork and commercial follow-up

Risk register (top items):
- Dataset quality: real customer transcripts contain many image/pdfs -> extra extraction work; mitigation: ask for initial 500 sample transcripts in text form asap
- Unexpected cost: early high QPS test runs produce higher than estimated token counts; mitigation: set budget guardrail and token caps on routes during testing
- SecOps blocks hosted logging: may force Private deployment for full PII flows; mitigation: plan for a minimal on-prem connector demo in Week 2 if required

Evaluation harness (deliverables):
- test-suite.sh: automated run for functional scenarios (SFTP -> ingest -> summarize -> validate against golden answers)
- perf-load.yml: k6/locust config files for 50/70 QPS runs
- small labeled dev set: 500 anonymized transcripts for triage intent labeling (S3 artifact)
- metrics dashboard: Redwood Console share link with latency/cost panels (view-only for CobaltBank)

Demo checklists (for the final stakeholder demo):
- Live run of three scenarios with CobaltBank sample data (pass/fail recorded)
- Display of 95p latency, error rates, and cost-per-1k tokens in dashboard
- Walkthrough of KMS-wrapped logs and audit entries for a sample request
- Failover simulation: trigger fallback region and show continuity of service

Open questions / decisions needed from CobaltBank:
- Do you want us to include encrypted transcript storage in Hosted demo or treat transcripts as ephemeral only? (decision deadline: Day 2)
- Which team owns the redaction rules? (POs: Legal vs Support)
- Is there an internal SOC2/attestation checklist we should run against before Week 2 load tests?

Notes to SEs (implementation tips / gotchas):
- Use prefix/KV caching aggressively for multi-turn triage flows to reduce repeated token decode costs
- Prefer smaller quantized variants for cheaper reranking passes; reserve higher-quality variant for final output step
- Record token-level traces for a subset of requests to troubleshoot 95p latency anomalies (store with KMS wrapping)

Contacts:
- CobaltBank PO: Jordan Whitaker <jordan.whitaker@cobaltbank.com>
- CobaltBank SecOps: Elena Varga <elena.varga@cobaltbank.com>
- Redwood SE lead: Ava Martinez <ava.m@redwood.ai>
- Redwood Infra: Marcus Green <marcus.g@redwood.ai>
- CS lead: Linnea Cho <linnea.c@redwood.ai>

Next steps (immediate):
- Schedule kickoff meeting (owner: Ava) — target 2024-11-06
- Customer to deliver 500-sample redacted transcript bundle by 2024-11-08
- SE to provision initial Hosted baseline tests by 2024-11-09

Quick wins to demonstrate early value:
- 1-click summarization demo from SFTP drop to generated summary within 30s for a sample file
- Live triage demo that routes a ticket to the correct intent with >85% precision on a small dev set

Appendix: example evaluation prompts (dev set snippets) — to be redacted before sharing externally:
- "Customer: I was double-charged for last month’s subscription, I need a refund." -> Expected triage intent: billing_refund
- "Customer: My account got locked after suspicious activity, I can’t log in." -> Expected triage intent: account_access
- Summarization gold sample: short bullet list of actionable next steps pulled from a 6-paragraph support interaction

---
Draft notes: this doc is intentionally pragmatic / checklist-first. SEs: add any missing test scripts into the GITHUB folder and flag open PRs in the linked_artifacts list.
